findings.criterion: with the three model classes configured on a non-default provider and `cfg.model` left on the default provider, NO call in review-plan, review, review-code or verify-completion resolves to the `cfg.model` provider — asserted from a run's usage log
findings.detail: `operations.py::review_ticket` (op=`ticket-quality`, the `rebar review` workflow) is intentionally left on raw `cfg.model` and registered in `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN`. Under Config B (classes on non-default provider, `cfg.model` on default provider), this call resolves to the `cfg.model` provider. The criterion says NO call in `review` should resolve to `cfg.model` provider, but `review_ticket` does by design. The last ticket comment acknowledges this inconsistency and recommends the revert, but the criterion itself was not updated to reflect the narrowed scope. Additionally, the criterion asks for assertion from a live run's usage log; no post-fix Config B run result is recorded in the ticket.

citations.description: review_ticket does not bind a class — uses raw cfg.model with documented reason

findings.criterion: each of the four sites selects its model from the class vocabulary, and the class chosen for each is stated in the code with its reason rather than left implicit
findings.detail: Three of the four original bypass sites now select from the class vocabulary (`enrich.py` → trivial, `overlap/judge.py` → standard, `code_review/workflow_ops.py` → standard), each with a documented reason. However, `operations.py::review_ticket` (op=`ticket-quality`) does NOT select from the class vocabulary — it uses raw `cfg.model` by design. The criterion requires all four sites to select from the class vocabulary. The implementation deliberately exempts `review_ticket`, which is a design decision documented in the code and test, but it means the criterion as written is not satisfied.
